summary: The Newark Herald, Vol. 11, No. 24, National Edition, 12-page issue, Saturday July 30, 1938. Unlike the July 23 and June 11 scans, this issue is Newark Herald throughout; no New Jersey Herald News section is bound with it. Front page covers the permanent closing of the Elizabeth Dowd Natatorium after an NAACP-led delegation refused a segregated-hours compromise; a fatal two-car crash on Route 29 that killed Newark cab starter William Gibbons and passenger Eddie Pollard; a controversy at the NJ State Federation of Colored Women's Clubs convention over remarks by WPA official Mrs. Elizabeth C. Denny Van about 'Mammy'; the North Jersey Baptist Association's Silver Jubilee convention parade honoring Dr. L. K. Williams; the Father Divine name case; and Hoot Gibson's indictment. Page 2 carries the Ku Klux Klan cross-burning and mob harassment of a Black family at the Fayson Lake development near Butler, NJ, under the head 'Hooded Mob Stirs Terror - Fiery Cross Burned in Front of House at Fayson Lake Development'; the Klan story is not a front-page item. National/international items include a fatal dynamite explosion killing ten Black workers on a Baltimore PWA water-tunnel project, NAACP secretary Walter White's Virgin Islands visit with Judge William H. Hastie, composer William Grant Still's World's Fair commission, and Governor A. Harry Moore's appointments to a state study commission on Negro living conditions. Extensive club, society, church, and sports pages cover Newark, Orange, Montclair, Summit, Hackensack, Vaux Hall, Jersey City, Bayonne, Nutley, Atlantic City and other NJ communities, plus Newark Eagles baseball, Henry Armstrong's title-fight training, and nightlife columns ('Mainly About Tan Town', 'Definitely About Jersey', 'Stuff & Nonsense').

incidents.what: Negro delegation led by Dr. William H. Brown refuses segregated-hours compromise; Elizabeth Recreation Commission votes to permanently close Dowd Natatorium for the season
Fatal head-on two-car crash on Route 29 in Union Township; William Gibbons and Eddie Pollard killed, four others injured

Mrs. Elizabeth C. Denny Van's 'Mammy' remark at the NJ Federation of Colored Women's Clubs convention in Bordentown draws protest from Mrs. Armeta H. Douglass. The convention was printed in advance as running July 20-23, 1938, so its only Wednesday was July 20; the earlier reading of July 27 falls after the convention closed
Mrs. Ida Brown of Jersey City elected president of NJ State Federation of Colored Women's Clubs, succeeding Mrs. Alice B. Arrington
North Jersey District Baptist Association Silver Jubilee parade through Newark's Third Ward honoring Dr. L. K. Williams
Ku Klux Klan burns cross and mob stones cottage at Fayson Lake development near Butler, NJ, after a Negro family moved in; reported on page 2, not the front page
500 pounds of dynamite explode prematurely in Loch Raven-Monte Bello water tunnel PWA project, Baltimore, killing ten Black workers
Father Divine disciple 'Faithful Mary' faces traffic-court case over using 'Divine' name on license/registration
Newark beauticians organize opposition to proposed city ordinance requiring early closing of beauty shops

connections: This scan is The Newark Herald only, 12 pages, Vol. 11, No. 24. It carries no New Jersey Herald News section, so items from it must not be attributed to the Herald News (publication id 16).
Society editor Lillian B. Huff and columnists Lou Blackmon and Tommy Watkins are recurring Newark Herald staff also referenced in the July 23 issue.
Coverage of NAACP national secretary Walter White and NJ NAACP branches (Elizabeth, state office under Dr. D. W. Anthony) links to national NAACP activity.
References the Negro Actors Guild of America (Ethel Waters presiding) consistent with the July 23 issue's mention of the Guild's newsletter editor Mrs. Geraldine Dismond.
Newark Eagles and Negro National League baseball coverage continues from the July 23 issue (Willie Wells, Mule Suttles, Ray Dandridge).
